title: The nonalgebraicity lemma omits a distinctness hypothesis.
details: Chernikov, Lecture Notes on Stability Theory (updated2017-08-27), Lemma2.31 printed pp.17–18, asserts that a point of an infinite indiscernible sequence is not algebraic over the other indexed points and the base parameters. Example2.27 explicitly permits constant sequences. In an infinite pure-equality structure, take a constant sequence with every entry b, and let the set of other indices contain one j. Its parameter set contains b, so b is in its algebraic closure, contradicting the lemma. Repair: require pairwise distinct entries (or tuple values in the tuple formulation); then the dense-order extension argument gives infinitely many distinct solutions of every relevant formula. This is adjacent source material; no unqualified nonalgebraicity claim is adopted.
